task.description: Letflow.SandboxPool's async DB worker (ISS-0224, Task.Supervisor.async_nolink/3 spawned from pump/1) returns an UNTYPED result to handle_info/2's clause A. complete_op/3 pattern-matches on exactly four (op-kind, result) shapes with NO catch-all clause -- if run_op/1 (via provision_sandbox/2 or drop_schema/1) ever returns a fifth shape, complete_op/3 raises FunctionClauseError inside a GenServer callback, crashing the single supervised pool process that holds ALL slot bookkeeping (active, waiting, db_queue, in_flight), with no reclaim and no cleanup for every in-flight claim. Design: (1) a closed, explicit type for the worker's legal return values: (2) a TOTAL handle_info/2 clause-A body -- every legal value routed to today's complete_op/3 path unchanged, every illegal value routed to a non-crashing recovery path, with reasoning for the chosen recovery (not just a declared mechanism); (3) a test design that deliberately drives an unexpected worker return and asserts the pool survives with slot bookkeeping intact (a subsequent claim/1 still works). Do NOT change INV-SP-A1 (reservation/quota), INV-SP-A2 (exactly-one-reply), INV-SP-A3 (ref classification), or the owner-monitor reclaim semantics -- read lib/letflow/design/iss0224-sandbox-pool-async-provisioning.md in full first; if the fix seemed to require touching any of those, stop and flag it as a blocking finding instead of proceeding (it does not). Design-artefact discipline: signatures, type shapes, and precise algorithm/test-case description only -- no .ex implementation bodies.
acceptance_criteria: A closed, explicit type is defined for run_op/1's legal return values (stated as a tagged-tuple union or a struct, with the choice justified)

handle_info/2's clause A is redesigned to be total over that type: every legal value reaches complete_op/3 exactly as today, every illegal value is caught by an explicit final case with no path that can raise FunctionClauseError
The recovery mechanism for an illegal value is specified with reasoning for why it is correct (not merely declared), and does not crash the pool
INV-SP-A1, INV-SP-A2, INV-SP-A3, and the owner-monitor reclaim semantics are explicitly confirmed unchanged, with a stated argument for each, not just an assertion

A precise test-case description exists that deliberately drives an unexpected run_op/1-equivalent return and asserts the pool survives with active/in_flight bookkeeping intact and a subsequent claim/1 still working
No implementation code (.ex bodies) is present in the design doc -- signatures and type shapes only

result.summary: Wrote lib/letflow/design/iss0226-sandbox-pool-worker-result-typing.md. Root cause re-derived from source: run_op/1 (sandbox_pool.ex:586-590) has no @spec: complete_op/3 (:597-665) is four exact-match clauses with no catch-all, so a fifth return shape raises FunctionClauseError inside handle_info/2 (a GenServer callback), crashing the single pool process holding all slot bookkeeping. Design: (1) a closed tagged-tuple union `@typep worker_result :: provision_result() | drop_result()` -- chosen over a wrapping struct because the four legal values already ARE these exact tuples/atoms today, so the type formalizes the existing shapes rather than requiring provision_sandbox/2, drop_schema/1, and complete_op/3's four clauses to be rewritten to unwrap a struct (would violate the no-touch scope on invariant-bearing code). (2) A new private `classify_worker_result(op, result) :: {:ok, worker_result()} | :invalid`, five clauses (four legal pairings + catch-all), called inside handle_info/2's clause A BEFORE complete_op/3; on {:ok, _} the existing complete_op/3 path runs completely unchanged (its own four clauses need no catch-all, since classify_worker_result/2 already guarantees only those four shapes reach it -- proof in doc section 4.3); on :invalid, logs the unexpected shape (op kind, sandbox_id, raw value) via Logger.error/1 and calls handle_worker_death/1 -- the SAME function clause-B case 1 already uses for an outright worker crash. Reasoning given (section 5): an unrecognized reply and a crash-without-returning are the same kind of uncertainty from the pool's perspective (unknown DB side-effect outcome), and handle_worker_death/1 already encodes the correct conservative recovery per op kind (compensating orphan-drop for a provision, {:error, :release_failed} reply for a release, unconditional in_flight clear) with an existing correctness proof this reuse inherits for free. Process.demonitor(ref, [:flush]) ordering preserved identically on both the valid and invalid branches (documented as load-bearing, section 4.2, to avoid a stray :DOWN(:normal) double-processing as a second death). Test design (section 7): :sys.replace_state/2 injects a well-formed in_flight entry with a fabricated task_ref (never attached to a real Task, so deterministic, no race), send(pool, {fake_ref, garbage}) drives the exact clause-A path, then asserts Process.alive?(pool), in_flight == nil, and a REAL subsequent claim/2 + release/2 round-trip succeeds end-to-end against a real DB -- proving recovery, not just survival. Companion case for the :drop/:release op kind included so both handle_worker_death/1 branches get regression coverage. Section 8 states the invariant-preservation argument for each of INV-SP-A1/A2/A3 and owner-monitor semantics explicitly (not merely asserted) -- none required touching, so no blocking finding was raised. No implementation code present -- signatures, @typep declarations, and algorithm/test-case prose only. Two open questions recorded (telemetry convention parity; provision_sandbox/2's rescue clause as the likeliest future source of a fifth shape) -- neither silently resolved.
result.next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR for the hard gate on this design.
